problem_text:
A manufacturing district aims to devise a resource‑conservation strategy to lower aggregate waste‑material discharge from a set of production lines. Initially, no mitigation techniques have been deployed.

The attributes of each production line are as follows:
* For Line 1, discharge coefficient is 1.913, throughput is 136.437.
* For Line 2, discharge coefficient is 2.945, throughput is 219.074.
* For Line 3, discharge coefficient is 2.175, throughput is 146.219.
* For Line 4, discharge coefficient is 1.346, throughput is 259.758.
* For Line 5, discharge coefficient is 1.808, throughput is 189.586.
* For Line 6, discharge coefficient is 2.251, throughput is 296.948.
* For Line 7, discharge coefficient is 0.738, throughput is 63.642.
* For Line 8, discharge coefficient is 2.154, throughput is 210.85.
* For Line 9, discharge coefficient is 1.121, throughput is 89.232.

Several recovery technologies are available, each characterized by a specific waste‑reduction rate:
* Technology1 diminishes discharge by 22%
* Technology2 diminishes discharge by 22%
* Technology3 diminishes discharge by 20%
* Technology4 diminishes discharge by 84%
* Technology5 diminishes discharge by 51%
* Technology6 diminishes discharge by 71%
* Technology7 diminishes discharge by 12%
* Technology8 diminishes discharge by 86%
* Technology9 diminishes discharge by 72%

Deploying a technology on a line introduces an extra expense per unit of throughput. The expense matrix for all line–technology pairings is given below:

| Line \ Technology | Tech1 | Tech2 | Tech3 | Tech4 | Tech5 | Tech6 | Tech7 | Tech8 | Tech9 |
|-------------------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| Line 1 | 132.23 | 86.623 | 54.65 | 97.228 | 162.24 | 95.139 | 172.752 | 94.943 | 32.554 |
| Line 2 | 104.501 | 134.141 | 29.502 | 88.344 | 115.855 | 10.032 | 27.27 | 124.799 | 127.623 |
| Line 3 | 67.874 | 106.584 | 49.302 | 137.58 | 190.567 | 79.035 | 20.312 | 52.354 | 96.347 |
| Line 4 | 116.429 | 127.754 | 99.895 | 134.862 | 146.024 | 31.664 | 154.271 | 52.132 | 74.858 |
| Line 5 | 167.678 | 193.242 | 65.477 | 109.177 | 143.398 | 18.698 | 41.19 | 36.685 | 146.203 |
| Line 6 | 147.096 | 30.323 | 126.062 | 45.633 | 186.741 | 84.65 | 96.839 | 158.47 | 146.19 |
| Line 7 | 30.475 | 88.749 | 186.059 | 169.119 | 121.874 | 156.708 | 95.596 | 135.107 | 191.676 |
| Line 8 | 35.581 | 104.777 | 110.769 | 19.229 | 187.709 | 169.375 | 101.757 | 106.583 | 185.021 |
| Line 9 | 43.668 | 119.925 | 148.794 | 34.393 | 83.607 | 124.104 | 177.712 | 105.781 | 83.086 |

The task is to decide which technologies to implement on each line (lines may adopt multiple technologies concurrently), and a line may also be left partially untreated if required.
The objective is to guarantee that the total waste discharge is curtailed by at least a fraction P = 0.69 of the baseline quantity, while minimizing the overall expenditure.
